messages:
Priya: Quick postmortem / notes from the multi-region evacuation preflight we ran last night. TL;DR: failover path worked end-to-end, but we observed KV cache priming lag and a client-affinity leak that created ~2s tail latencies for ~1% of requests. Please skim and react with :eyes: if you were on call.

Alex: I captured the runbook and timings from the run. Uploading raw timings below.

Alex: ```
# preflight evac runbook (simplified)
1) mark region B read-only: api call -> /control/regions/B/mode=readonly
2) pre-drain warmup: send 100k requests with residency hint to B (30m)
3) start drain: /control/regions/B/drain?timeout=900
4) cut traffic: update route table cluster-side -> prefer A
5) validate: per-route p99 latency, kv-cache hit ratio, lease counts
```

Alex: Observed timings: pre-drain warmup 28m, full drain 7m, route switch propagation 18s.

Jin: Reproduced the affinity leak on a small harness. Root cause: our proxy retry logic retains X-Region hint when it retries across a backend host. When the retry crosses a staging proxy that serves region A, the header shouldn't be forwarded. Patch sketched: clear header on cross-proxy retry.

Jin: snippet: ```diff
- forward_headers += request.headers['X-Region']
+ if not is_cross_proxy_retry: forward_headers += request.headers['X-Region']
```

Mateo: The KV cache priming lag looks like a slow cold set after the warmup. Warmup load was hitting cache but TTLs were shorter than we thought (config drift). Two options: extend warmup duration or set transient TTL=600s during evacuation. I prefer changing TTL in the orchestration layer so warmup is effective.

Priya: Interesting — did we track which tenants were impacted? I saw the tail latencies concentrated on high-cardinality tenants.

Alex: Yes, top 3 tenants by QPS accounted for 72% of the affected requests. They had lots of short lived session keys.

Mateo: For the TTL flip we can do this atomically via the control-plane API: `POST /control/cache/ttl?scope=evac&value=600` and then revert post-cutover. Suggest adding a guarded flag so it only applies during preflight windows.

ops-bot: deploy-notify: canary service `proxy-v2` deployed to region A at 2024-11-02T03:14Z :white_check_mark:

canary-bot: perf-check: route switch p50/p95/p99 = 12ms / 110ms / 560ms (during switch) ; KV hit ratio dropped from 98% -> 82% for 2.5m windows.

Jin: Another observation: client SDKs that pin on first contact didn't update `X-Client-Region` on the retry path, so some clients continued to send region B hints after the routing change. We should add a TTL on client-region cookies and document the SDK behavior.

Priya: Action items I propose: 
- [Priya] Draft a short runbook appendix for the warmup TTL flip and guard flag.
- [Alex] Add a preflight check that asserts `kv_hit_ratio >= 95%` OR fail the evacuation.
- [Jin] Submit the proxy retry header patch and include unit tests.
- [Mateo] Add a canary flag to the cache TTL API and a revert task.
- [All] Add a client-SDK note about region hint TTL.

Alex: I'll open the follow-up PRs and link them here.

Priya: One more design question: long-term, do we want to decouple lease ownership from region hints so a transient proxy change doesn't rely on header forwarding? Pros: fewer accidental affinity leaks. Cons: more control-plane coordination. Thoughts?

Mateo: I favour decoupling: introduce a lightweight ownership token per-tenant stored in control-plane that proxies can fetch, with local caching. That avoids relying solely on headers. Risks: extra control-plane QPS and cache staleness. We can mitigate with short TTL and backoff.

Jin: Agree with decouple for safety. Implementation roadmap: 1) prototyping via control-plane token, 2) pilot with a subset of tenants, 3) measure added control-plane load.

Priya: OK — let's treat the token work as a cross-team RFC (eng-runtime + infra + product). For now, the preflight checklist and patch + TTL flip are highest priority.

Priya: If nobody objects, I'll assign owners and update the evacuation runbook. Thanks for the quick turnaround. :heart:

Alex: :thumbsup:

Mateo: Adding the TTL API PR to my queue, aiming EOD tomorrow.

Jin: Will have proxy patch review ready in ~6h.

ops-bot: incident-sim: simulation record uploaded -> s3://redwood-sims/evac/4765432999/summary.log

Priya: Great. I'll follow up with the RFC invite for the token work next week and post updated runbook once PRs land.
